reason: E1 shows ML potentials can achieve near-DFT accuracy for energies and forces in a refractory high-entropy alloy, supporting the premise that a limited training set can capture key interactions. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that such potentials retain anharmonicity and electron-vibration coupling in free-energy calculations, that the coupled MC/free-energy workflow is faster than TOR-TILD, or that it achieves the claimed 5% accuracy for fusion properties. E2 discusses vibrational entropy from AIMD but does not validate the proposed ML+MC workflow.
premises: ML potentials trained on short AIMD can capture anharmonicity and electron-vibration coupling
ML potentials can be trained on limited configurational ensembles for multicomponent systems
Monte Carlo or free-energy integration with ML potentials is faster than explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD
The approach yields fusion free energies within ~5% of full AIMD results
